Definition: to hide (by covering), literally or figuratively
BiblicalUsage: Çâthar means to hide by covering, and it runs both ways in Scripture: men hide from God, and God hides His people. Elijah was hidden by the brook Cherith, and the child Joash was hidden in the house of God while the queen sought his life. Hiding can be fear, and it can be refuge; the word covers both.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God is both the one we hide from and the one we hide in. Çâthar shows the difference: hiding from Him is fear, and hiding in Him is safety, and I know which one I want.
